A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adalina framework, despite the changed title. Their main sections, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original approximation-error experiments on six datasets, including comparisons with baselines and sampling/adaptivity analyses in Figures 1–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports original approximation-error experiments on twelve datasets, including revised analyses and additional benchmark results in Figures 1–7 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain their sampling distributions and adaptive updates. However, Section 4 adds a concrete adaptation for combining Adalina with paired sampling: run it on (U−Uc)/2 using half as many sampled subsets, avoiding the cancellation caused by directly inserting complementary samples.

E1.justification: The six original datasets are retained, while jannis, wave energy, BT, har, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR10 small are added and evaluated in Figures 6–7. This expands represented domains to activity recognition and image data and raises the largest feature count from 308 to 3,072 (Table 1).

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MSR-Banzhaf, MSR-Prob, SHAP-IQ, unbiased kernelSHAP, linear-space AME, ARM, GELS, and GELS-Shapley. Figure 1's 'modified' sampling is renamed 'geomean' without changing the comparator. The added datasets use the existing comparator pool.

E3.justification: The evaluation design is retained, but reported settings change: generally five boosting trees in v1 become ten in v2, with fifty specified for Figure 1's mixed-sign utilities. New har and Fashion-MNIST experiments use 100 queries per player, and CIFAR small uses 20; other datasets retain 1,000.

E4.justification: Existing analyses are revised under the changed utility models: Figure 1's sampling comparison uses a fifty-tree mixed-sign case, and Figures 2–3 update gamma sensitivity and fixed-versus-adaptive centering evidence. These retain their original questions. Figures 6–7 add benchmark comparisons rather than new robustness or ablation questions.

E5.justification: Both versions average results over ten random seeds, report standard deviations, and fix other randomness to 2026. The additional plots follow the same uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many error curves in Figures 1–5 are replaced, and Figures 6–7 add results for six datasets. For example, Figure 4's FOTP weighted-Banzhaf errors for AME and MSR-Prob increase with weight in v1 but decrease in v2. These changed findings accompany revised tree models and do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 and Appendix A revise the query-bound coefficient from 16 to 36 and explicitly derive the range 0<epsilon<=2C. The introduction replaces possibly dependent estimates with an i.i.d. assumption. Sections 3–4 add exact paired-sampling improvement conditions, including a covariance formulation. The central complexity orders, MSE bound, and framework derivations remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: sharper query complexities, connections among existing estimators, characterization of paired sampling, and adaptive linear-space estimation with provably improved MSE. The title change and additional experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains that naive pairing makes the estimated centering vector zero, cancelling Adalina's adaptivity, and discusses how to avoid this failure. It also explicitly connects SHAP-IQ's nonoptimal sampling to Figure 3's performance. Existing qualifications about nonsymmetric semi-values and kernelSHAP's potential Shapley-value advantage remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides an Adalina code link and identifies the numerically stable TreeGrad ground-truth implementation with its code link. Table 1 adds dataset sources and tree depths for the new experiments. v1 already documented both algorithms, software classes, seeds, and original dataset settings.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges concurrent paired-sampling work by Fumagalli et al. (2026), adds exchangeable-pair concentration references and ground-truth/dataset citations, and exempts least-squares estimators from an earlier blanket statement about biased-estimator analyses. Its principal positioning relative to OFA, kernelSHAP, SHAP-IQ, and regression adjustment remains intact.

P1.justification: The title becomes 'Adalina: Adaptive Linear Approximation for the Shapley Value and Beyond.' Conference front matter, acknowledgments, and an impact statement are added, alongside localized language corrections and explanations. The six-section narrative and Appendices A–C retain their organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds two appendix multipanel figures and expands Table 1 using the existing formats. Algorithm 1 and Figure 5 relocate, and existing plots receive axis and legend adjustments, including 'modified' becoming 'geomean.' The overall visual design and corresponding figure structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves rigor through the revised concentration-bound derivation and explicit paired-sampling conditions, broadens empirical support to higher-dimensional activity and image datasets, and provides more reproducibility information. These strengthen an already developed framework without changing its central conclusions. Changed tree settings limit direct performance comparisons between versions.
